posts.title: teste fenix
posts.sub: Why the Brazilian luxury consumer rewards restraint.
posts.body:
The instinct when entering a new market is to be seen everywhere at once. In Brazil, that instinct quietly erodes value.

The sophisticated consumer here reads over-exposure as a lack of confidence. A maison that is suddenly on every shelf, every feed, every influencer, signals availability rather than desire. And desire is the entire product.

We build presence the other way around: scarcity, the right rooms, the right voices, the right three retailers before the right three hundred. Visibility is easy to buy. Desirability has to be earned, and it compounds.

posts.title: The Timeline No Maison Plans For
posts.sub: Regulation, customs, and the six months hiding in your launch.
posts.body:
Every international brand I meet has a launch date in mind. Very few have accounted for what sits between the decision and the shelf.

Registration, labelling, ANVISA, customs, local distribution agreements: each is manageable on its own, and each quietly adds weeks. Skipped or rushed, they surface later as seized shipments and delayed launches, at the worst possible moment.

Market access is not a formality you handle at the end. It is the architecture you design from the first conversation. Done right, it disappears; done late, it becomes the whole story.
